title: Quickstart landing visuals redesign: hero, flow diagrams, and step cards
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Refresh the Quickstart landing page visual assets to improve clarity, reduce time-to-first-success, and better reflect recent product UX changes. This ticket covers hero imagery, a simplified onboarding flow diagram, and the set of step cards used in docs and the product console.

Goals:
- Create a hero that communicates "Redwood makes LLM inference production-ready" with clear CTA focus for both new users and returning engineers.
- Produce a modular onboarding flow diagram (desktop + stacked mobile variants) that can be used across docs, Console onboarding modals, and marketing pages.
- Design step card components (3 sizes) with accessible color contrast, microcopy guidelines, and placeholders for screenshots or terminal snippets.
- Deliver assets in Figma + exported PNGs/SVGs and one Lottie prototype for the animated hero variation.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Hero art: two visual directions (metaphor-driven illustration vs. UI-centered montage), header layout variants (left-aligned copy, center-aligned), mobile breakpoints, and a Lottie animation for hero attention state.
- Onboarding flow diagram: simplified 4-step flow (API key -> Quickstart template -> Run sample -> Inspect traces), annotated for engineers, and redlines for dev. Provide SVG + responsive slices.
- Step cards: primary (feature highlight), compact (inline docs), and wide (full-width console banner). Provide copy examples, state variations (default, hover, success, loading), and accessibility checks.
- Updated product screenshots: capture Console quickstart run with new callout overlays (bounding boxes and microcopy). Provide obfuscated tenant IDs.
- Handoff package: Figma file, exported assets, implementation notes (tokens, spacing, responsive rules), component tokens for engineering.

Acceptance criteria:
- Two hero directions reviewed and approved by PM and Marketing (approval recorded in comments).
- Flow diagram SVG renders cleanly at 320px, 768px, and 1440px widths without information loss.
- Step cards meet WCAG AA for contrast and have keyboard-focus mockups.
- Dev has a documented index of exported assets and implementation notes in the handoff doc.
- Related PRs created that reference this ticket and link to the Figma frames.

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Illustration vs UI montage: Illustration communicates concept faster but may require additional copy to surface product specifics. UI montage is literal but risks becoming out-of-date with rapid Console UI iterations. We'll deliver both to let PM/Marketing pick.
- Lottie hero animation should be subtle; primary CTA must remain visible even during animation for accessibility.

Notes for implementation:
- Use design tokens: h-spacing-24 for hero padding, grid-12 for desktop.
- Screenshot exports should use background-blur to mask customer data and a 4px rounded rect crop.
- Step cards will be implemented as responsive components; provide states and aria-label suggestions in handoff doc.

Files and links are in design_links/attachments below.
